chunks: A man said to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام: “O cousin of the best of Allah’s creation, what is the meaning of raising your right foot and placing down your left in the tashahhud?”
He said: “Its interpretation is: O Allah, cause falsehood to die and establish the truth.”
He said: “Then what is the meaning of the Imam’s saying: al-salāmu ʿalaykum?”

So he said: “Indeed, the Imam conveys on behalf of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and says in his conveying to the people of the congregation: safety for you from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.”

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony portion of salat (prayer) in which specific declarations are recited while seated
key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ: the salutation of peace concluding the prayer
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the prayer leader speaking on behalf of the congregation
key_terms.الْبَاطِلَ: falsehood, that which is invalid or opposed to truth
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: the truth, that which is firmly established and right

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of raising the right foot in tashahhud and the Imam’s salām in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains inner meanings connected to acts and words within salat (prayer), especially the posture of tashahhud and the concluding salām. It presents these ritual elements as bearing theological significance: the triumph of truth over falsehood and a declaration of safety from punishment on the Day of Resurrection for the congregation.
